documents: ID proof of complainant
Proof of purchase (invoice/receipt/bill)
Warranty/guarantee card if any
Correspondence with opposite party (emails, letters, screenshots)
Proof of amount paid (bank statement/payment receipt)
Notice sent to opposite party, if any
consumer.fee_rule: Nil up to Rs 5 lakh; slab-wise court fee thereafter per Consumer Protection (Consumer Commission Procedure) Regulations 2020, payable via e-Daakhil.
consumer.deadline_rule: 2 years from the date the cause of action arose (Section 69, Consumer Protection Act 2019).

police.portal_note: No online portal: Nearest police station / SP office; MP Police citizen portal https://mppolice.gov.in for e-FIR of vehicle theft
documents: ID proof of complainant
Any evidence of the offence (photos, videos, medical report, bills)
Ownership documents (for theft of vehicle/property)
Witness names and contact details, if any
police.fee_rule: No fee for lodging an FIR.
police.deadline_rule: No limitation for cognizable offences; file immediately.

tenant.portal_note: Rent Controlling Authority Bhopal / civil court
documents: Rent/lease agreement
Rent receipts / bank payment proof
Security deposit receipt
Notice received from landlord/tenant, if any
Photographs of premises/disputed condition
tenant.fee_rule: Court fee as per MP Court Fees Act, nominal for rent applications; varies by relief sought.
tenant.deadline_rule: Reply within notice period; 3 years for money claims under Limitation Act.

labour.portal_note: Labour Commissioner, Madhya Pradesh (Shram Seva / Shramik Sewa portal) and the district Labour Office; claims under the Payment of Wages Act go to the notified Authority / Labour Court, PF grievances to EPFiGMS (epfigms.gov.in) and the EPFO Regional Office Indore or Bhopal
documents: ID proof of the worker (Aadhaar) and, if issued, the employer's ID card or gate pass
Appointment letter, contract or any written terms of employment
Wage slips, wage register extract or bank statement showing salary credits
Proof of the period worked (attendance record, muster roll entry, biometric log)
Termination or relieving letter, or a note of the date and manner of dismissal if none was given
EPFO member passbook / UAN statement and ESIC contribution history, if PF or ESI is in issue
Copy of the demand letter sent to the employer and its postal/email delivery proof
labour.fee_rule: No court fee on a worker's application to the Authority under the Payment of Wages Act 1936 or the Minimum Wages Act 1948; no fee for a complaint to the Labour Commissioner, EPFO or ESIC.
labour.deadline_rule: 12 months from the date the wages fell due (Payment of Wages Act 1936, s.15(2)); 6 months for a minimum-wage claim (Minimum Wages Act 1948, s.20(2)); 3 years from the date of termination for a direct application to the Labour Court (Industrial Disputes Act 1947, s.2A(3)); gratuity is payable within 30 days and the application to the Controlling Authority is ordinarily within 90 days thereafter (Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, s.7).
